title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared to blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the preregistered harmful-change mapping and all per-episode traces required to compute that aggregation are archived and their locations are documented in Methods so independent auditors can reproduce the preregistered safety aggregation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that interposing deterministic verifiers can raise verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps emphasize that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse, and intervention informativeness is a known methodological risk: a verifier-guided intervention can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. To ensure the intervention was meaningfully exercised we used a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired design that shares the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Controlled and empirical GVR results in adjacent domains show that deterministic verifier diagnostics can materially improve verifier pass rates on program, IaC, and DSL tasks, while also revealing exploitation risks and interaction overheads. Representative works: Cadenas proposes a generate-verify-repair architecture for deterministic validation in regulated code-generation settings and documents pipeline-level tradeoffs [1]; Jouini evaluates verifier-first designs for IaC and shows gains but domain dependence [2]; Gupta presents controlled analyses of verifier-exploitation pathologies in iterative refinement [3]; Sah et al. quantify a "verifier tax"—interaction and resource costs introduced by verifier-mediated workflows [4]; and Bilal et al. synthesize NetOps/AIOps surveys and field evidence underscoring read-vs-write safety distinctions [5]. These records motivated our controlled challenge, paired shared-candidate semantics, and preregistered harmful-change schema.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success requires both a deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministic controlled-fault candidate from deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1 was produced and reused across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40.

Model configuration and per-call sampling records. The archived model configuration declares declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset) in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call runtime sampling parameters and provider traces required for auditing are archived in the evidence bundle: per-call provider traces are available at execution/provider_calls/*.json and aggregated provider-call accounting appears in execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The execution manifest also records total hosted-model calls used = 118 (maximum_model_calls = 120) and stage-level counts (valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39). These archived per-call records permit independent verification of actual sampling and call metadata.

Controlled-challenge and missingness rules. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered 40 deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) injecting realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change). The execution manifest records controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 = 8d0879872348ae94a45f3d674df57d6552624cd841b62ab239a280347f5275c6 and source_generation_attempt_count = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' missingness rule excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; this occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv. Sensitivity analyses treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered.

Scoring and preregistered harmful-change mapping. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistered harmful-change labeling schema designates an episode harmful if its validation_after.violation_codes includes PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; the transformation artifact implementing this mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json. Per-episode validator traces (validation_after.violation_codes) required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; exact artifact locations and the compact operational mapping are provided for independent reconstruction (see Results).

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial) on the combined success predicate. We report discordant-pair counts, absolute risk difference, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity: single predefined primary test; subgroup analyses exploratory. All raw per-episode artifacts and scoring traces are archived for deterministic recomputation (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Analysis artifacts analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv are archived with SHA-256 hashes in the evidence bundle.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The paired table is archived at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (artifact hash recorded in the evidence bundle).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source-generation was invalid and produced two unscorable condition episodes (both_missing_pairs = 1). Per-episode terminal error reasons and logs are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis bounding harmful-overrepair. The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Therefore we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim. To enable exact independent reproduction of the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation from the archived artifacts we provide the compact operational mapping and precise artifact locations: (1) harmful-change labeling rule — label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; (2) per-episode records with validation_after.violation_codes are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl; (3) the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json and listed in the full artifact manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Reproduction steps: iterate the 39 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), read validation_after.violation_codes for each condition from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), apply the mapping to produce a harmful indicator per episode, then compute paired counts and the preregistered paired statistic per the analysis plan. All required per-episode fields and transformation artifacts are present in the archive; because the archived confirmatory executor omitted this aggregation, the preregistered harmful-overrepair verdict remains unresolved in this manuscript.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-pair JSON scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json, etc.). Example diagnostics illustrate typical mechanisms: validator_trace.violation_codes identify protected fields or unintended-state changes that guided guarded repairs to target corrective edits while blind repair sometimes omitted required restores. These per-episode traces support a plausible causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved post-repair verifier outcomes.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. The preregistered paired result indicates that exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics can materially increase verifier+simulator-validated success on the tested controlled-fault bank under shared controlled-candidate pairing. The paired design isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics because both arms used the same initial candidate and identical repair budgets; the observed discordant-pair pattern (n10 = 9 guarded-only successes vs n01 = 1 baseline-only success) suggests targeted corrections enabled by diagnostic exposure.

Safety boundary and unresolved confirmatory safety aggregation. Crucially, the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; the harmonic-change mapping and per-episode traces needed to compute it are archived and we provide the exact reconstruction path. Because the preregistered safety aggregation is absent from the archived confirmatory summary, we treat harmful-overrepair as unresolved for the confirmatory claim and make the artifacts available for deterministic reaggregation by auditors.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier-guided design increases interaction steps: hosted-model calls used = 118 with stage counts recorded in the execution manifest. These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but the present controlled experiment does not generalize cost/latency to production. Practitioners should ensure verifier coverage for critical safety properties, instrument harmful-change indicators (for example using the provided mapping), budget for verifier-mediated call counts, and validate under realistic task distributions before closed-loop deployment.

Verifier-exploitation and generality. Prior work documents verifier-exploitation risk when optimizing to a single proxy verifier; our short-horizon paired design and limited repair budget reduce exposure but do not eliminate long-horizon pathologies. Recommended mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, enforced harmful-change constraints (the preregistered mapping is an example), calibrated abstention, and UQ/uncertainty integration. External validity is limited: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank, and archived verifier/simulator restrict generalization to diverse vendor devices and live operator streams.

Reproducibility and auditability. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation manifests required to reproduce the primary and preregistered secondary aggregations are archived. Key artifact locations: execution/raw_results.jsonl (raw per-episode records), execution/scoring/*.json (per-episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/transformation_manifest.json (frozen harmful-change mapping), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv (archived analysis outputs), and execution/model_configuration.json (declared model settings). The evidence bundle includes artifact hashes and execution manifest pointers enabling deterministic independent recomputation.
sections.conclusion:
In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model gpt-5-mini, and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved; the archived artifacts and transformation manifest provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction. We release the full artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

[2] M. Jouini, "Verifier-First Evaluation of Agentic LLMs for Infrastructure-as-Code Generation," arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.20478, 2026. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20478.

[4] T. Sah, V. Srivastava, D. Sah, K. Jordan, "The Verifier Tax: Horizon Dependent Safety Success Tradeoffs in Tool Using LLM Agents," arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.19328, 2026. Available: http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19328.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json; per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived at execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
